Activation of the adiponectin-adiponectin receptor (AdipoR) axis directly counteracts these processes by stimulating adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent metabolic rebalancing, restoring mitochondrial fusion–fission homeostasis, enhancing oxidative capacity, reducing inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS-) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase-mediated injury, improving endothelial nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, and enhancing microvascular perfusion. In animal models, adiponectin or its mimetics consistently reduced infarct size, improved myocardial function, and attenuated apoptosis, inflammation, and no-reflow. A growing array of therapeutic strategies has emerged, each bringing its own pharmacologic nuances and implications for translation to the clinic. This review summarizes current strategies to enhance adiponectin action, highlights the progress in peptide and small-molecule mimetics, and discusses future directions for clinical translation in cardiometabolic diseases.

title: Navigating the landscape of stem cell therapeutics: Overcoming translational hurdles via emerging technologies and regulatory frontiers
abstract: Global population aging has increased the incidence of intractable diseases. Accordingly, regenerative medicine using stem cell therapies offers a critical shift from symptom management to functional tissue restoration. Hematopoietic, mesenchymal, and pluripotent stem cells (embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells) have shown promising therapeutic potential. However, their clinical translation is constrained by persistent biological, manufacturing, and regulatory hurdles associated with genomic instability, tumorigenic risk, and batch-to-batch heterogeneity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current stem cell research landscape, highlighting the strategic shift from traditional cell-centric development to a multi-disciplinary and technology-driven approach. Emerging technologies, including three-dimensional organoids, advanced biomaterials, genome editing, and artificial intelligence-integrated automated manufacturing, are actively resolving long-standing translational bottlenecks to ensure scalable, safe, and reproducible clinical implementation. Regulatory approaches differ across major countries; however, the trend toward incorporating patient needs is growing. This has accelerated access to innovative therapies, with ongoing efforts to ensure that these advances do not compromise safety or efficacy. Moving forward, the successful clinical integration of next-generation stem cell therapeutics is likely to be shaped by the synergy between harmonized regulatory requirements and reliable real-world evidence. Collectively, these factors serve to bridge the transition from early patient access to definitive licensing.

title: Nucleic acid therapeutics for reinvigorating p53 function in glioblastoma: concepts, limitations and recent advances
abstract: IDH-wildtype, high-grade glioma with predominantly astrocytic differentiation and classified as glioblastoma in the current WHO classification of central nervous system tumors is among the most common and aggressive primary malignant brain tumors. Glioblastoma remains largely refractory to current therapies, leading to early recurrence and poor prognosis. In nearly all glioblastomas, the p53 tumor-suppressor pathway is functionally inactivated, either through TP53 mutations or through deregulated signaling pathways that promote p53 degradation. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of gene therapy strategies designed to restore p53 function or exploit p53 loss-of-function in glioblastoma. In particular, it critically discusses the biological barriers and technical limitations of viral and non-viral nucleic acid delivery systems that have contributed to inadequate clinical outcomes, while also highlighting recent advances with potential to reinvigorate p53 function in glioblastoma.

title: Pharmacological targeting of ANO1/TMEM16A in cancer: from channel inhibition to protein downregulation
